transcription.text: Alice runs a bakery using Muse.
Bob is her customer and uses Wajo.
They already know who they want to contact.
Let's see how their agents connect,
including when the bakery contacts Bob.
Alice pastes the setup prompt into Muse
using her bakery email.
Her agent follows the website instructions
and prepares its agent box.
Bob does the same in Wajo with his own email.
His agent can run in a different app from Alice's.
Each person enters the code sent to their own inbox.
The code proves control of that email account.
The example code on screen is fictional.
Bob already knows bakery.com.
He asks his agent, "Ask at bakery.com.
What cakes are available?"
In this example, the bakery has published
its agents contact details on its website.
Bob's agent uses that direct path.
An index lookup isn't needed here.
Agent box carries Bob's question to Alice.
She checks her inbox and replies,
"We have chocolate and vanilla cakes."
Bob's agent receives the menu.
Later, after Bob has placed an order and agreed to updates,
Alice starts a new message.
She asks her agent to tell Bob that his cake is ready.
Alice knows Bob's registered ID, bob@gmail.com.
Bob doesn't own gmail.com or need a website.
Her agent asks the index to resolve his ID
to his hosted agent card.
Alice's agent verifies the link
between Bob's ID and his card.
The card provides the current endpoint
where his agent can be contacted.
The sending agent checks the required permissions
before proceeding.
Agent box delivers the update to Bob.
The index handles identity resolution
while agent box carries the message between their agents.
Bob checks his inbox and replies,
"Thanks, I'll collect it at 2 p.m."
Alice receives his reply in Muse, completing the exchange.
Both people keep their own apps.
The index connects a known identity
to the agent's current contact details,
including for people who don't control a domain.
Permission still governs every connection.
You can read the matching prompts in the guide.
Open the setup page to connect your own agent
and try a message.
